title: Summit Reserve Analysis Note: Kept Amount of a Returned Hazard Premium
content:
The kept amount of a returned hazard premium on a Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve under Set-Aside Accounts is defined from the reserve's hazard insurance bills, its ledger, its annual charges on file and its balance on the handling date.

**The withdrawn term and its payment.** The withdrawn hazard term is the withdrawn hazard insurance bill on file with the latest due date, which is the day that term began. The reserve's payment of it is the reserve's hazard insurance payment made against that bill.

**Time in force.** The cancellation date is the due date of the latest paid hazard insurance bill when that date is on or after the day the withdrawn term began, and otherwise the handling date. The days in force are the calendar days from the day the withdrawn term began to the cancellation date; the months in force are the whole calendar months between those dates; neither is below zero.

**Unearned premium.** The unearned hazard premium is the reserve's payment of the withdrawn term times the policy-year days, 365, less the days in force, divided by 365.

**Horizon and need.** The reserve period left is the plan's reserve months (shown in the plan matrix) less the whole calendar months from the reserve's established date to the handling date, never below zero, and the horizon of the hazard refund review is that many whole months. The tax part of the hazard refund need is the annual property tax on file times the horizon months divided by twelve. The insurance part is the annual hazard premium plus the annual flood premium on file, times the horizon months divided by twelve. The hazard refund need is the tax part plus the insurance part plus the hazard refund cushion, and the hazard refund cushion is zero.

**Room, excess and release.** The hazard refund room is the need less the reserve balance, never below zero; the hazard refund excess is the unearned hazard premium less the room, never below zero. A hazard refund excess above zero that is at least the release floor of 50.00 is released to the borrower's side; a smaller excess stays in the reserve. The borrower's side keeps the whole released excess.

**Result.** The kept amount of a returned hazard premium is the unearned hazard premium less the part of the released excess the borrower's side keeps, rounded half up to the cent once, at the end.

### Worked figures on hypothetical inputs

A reserve paid 1,460.00 against a hazard bill whose term began on 1 March; that bill is now withdrawn and no paid hazard bill is due on or after 1 March. Handling date 1 June: the cancellation date is the handling date, the days in force are 92, and the unearned premium is 1,460.00 times 273, divided by 365, which is 1,092.00. Annual charges on file: tax 3,000.00, hazard 1,500.00, flood 600.00; suppose the reserve period left is 4 months. Tax part 1,000.00, insurance part 700.00, need 1,700.00.

| Reserve balance | Room | Excess | Released | Kept amount |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1,000.00 | 700.00 | 392.00 | 392.00 | 700.00 |
| 660.00 | 1,040.00 | 52.00 | 52.00 | 1,040.00 |
| 650.00 | 1,050.00 | 42.00 | none (below 50.00) | 1,092.00 |
